title: Replying from an async hook does not halt the chain when 2+ async onSend hooks are registered
body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure it has not already been reported

### Fastify version

5.12.5

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

22.23.2

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

Fedora (container: node:22-slim)

### Description

Replying from an `async` lifecycle hook stops the chain as documented — **unless the application has two or more `async` `onSend` hooks registered.** In that case the route handler runs anyway.

[The docs](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/docs/Reference/Hooks.md#respond-to-a-request-from-a-hook) say:

> Replying from a hook implies that the hook chain is **stopped** and the rest of the hooks and handlers are not executed. [...] If the hook is `async`, `reply.send()` **must** be called *before* the function returns or the promise resolves, otherwise, the request will proceed.

In the reproduction below `reply.send()` *is* called before the async hook returns, so the chain should stop. It does for 0 or 1 `onSend` hooks, and does not for 2 or more.

The client still receives the body sent by the hook, so the only visible symptom is the **status code**, which the handler overwrites on an already-sent reply. That makes it easy to miss: we ran this in production for some time, and only noticed when one route returned `400` carrying a `401` body.

I appreciate `return reply` is the recommended form and fixes it. The bug is that the outcome depends on how many `async onSend` hooks are registered elsewhere in the app — a hook authored in one place changes the halting semantics of hooks everywhere else.

### Steps to Reproduce

```js
import Fastify from 'fastify'

async function run (onSendCount) {
  const app = Fastify()
  let handlerRan = false

  for (let i = 0; i < onSendCount; i++) {
    app.addHook('onSend', async (req, reply, payload) => payload)
  }

  app.get('/', {
    preHandler: async (req, reply) => {
      reply.code(401).send({ error: 'unauthorized' })
      // reply.send() called before the async hook returns
    },
    handler: async (req, reply) => {
      handlerRan = true
      return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'handler ran' })
    }
  })

  const res = await app.inject({ method: 'GET', url: '/' })
  await app.close()
  console.log(`onSend hooks=${onSendCount}  handlerRan=${handlerRan}  status=${res.statusCode}  body=${res.body}`)
}

for (const n of [0, 1, 2, 3]) await run(n)
```

Output on 5.12.5:

```
onSend hooks=0  handlerRan=false  status=401  body={"error":"unauthorized"}
onSend hooks=1  handlerRan=false  status=401  body={"error":"unauthorized"}
onSend hooks=2  handlerRan=true   status=400  body={"error":"unauthorized"}
onSend hooks=3  handlerRan=true   status=400  body={"error":"unauthorized"}
```

Note the body stays `unauthorized` while the status becomes `400`.

**Narrowing it down.** Both conditions are required — the replying hook must be `async`, and there must be ≥2 `async` `onSend` hooks:

```
BROKEN  2 async onSend,    async preHandler
ok      2 callback onSend, async preHandler
ok      1 async + 1 callback onSend, async preHandler
ok      2 async onSend,    callback preHandler
ok      2 async onRequest (instead of onSend), async preHandler
ok      2 async preValidation (instead of onSend), async preHandler
```

So it is specific to the count of **async** `onSend` hooks; the same number of `onRequest` or `preValidation` hooks does not trigger it, and callback-style `onSend` hooks do not either.

**It is not limited to `preHandler`.** With 2 async `onSend` hooks registered, replying from any async request hook lets the handler run:

```
BROKEN  replying from async onRequest
BROKEN  replying from async preParsing
BROKEN  replying from async preValidation
BROKEN  replying from async preHandler
```

### Expected Behavior

The handler should not run, and the response should be `401`, regardless of how many `onSend` hooks are registered — as the documentation states.

If sending without `return reply` from an async hook is considered unsupported, I think it would help to say so unconditionally in the docs, since today it works in the common case and silently changes behaviour once a second async `onSend` hook is added anywhere in the application.
